children: said Nov. 13 it has discussed buying approximately 1,200 acres managed by the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department around its launch facility near Boca Chica Beach, with roughly 600 acres to be protected under a permanent conservation easement. The company said the proposed purchase excludes the beach and coastline, which would remain public.
For investors, the proposal concerns security and land use around SpaceX’s

Starship launch operations. Acquiring the surrounding property could give the company greater control over access near its facility, while the conservation commitment would limit development on part of the land. The announcement did not disclose a purchase price, transaction timetable or financial impact.

said unauthorized visitors have entered operational areas through state-managed land, creating safety concerns around launch-site activities. It said it is working with the parks department and the Texas Department of Public Safety to improve access controls while maintaining public access to Boca Chica Beach.

The company described the proposed acquisition area as largely mudflats and coastal dunes without established hiking trails, campsites or recreational facilities. It said a permanent conservation easement would prohibit development on approximately 600 acres.

said proceeds from a sale would allow Texas to acquire other parkland and expand recreational opportunities in the Rio Grande Valley. The announcement did not identify replacement properties or provide a statement from the parks department confirming terms of a potential agreement.

said it has offered to invest tens of millions of dollars in efforts to address erosion at Boca Chica Beach in partnership with the Texas General Land Office. The announcement didn't provide a schedule or detailed funding terms for that work.

title: SpaceX outlines land purchase proposal near Boca Chica Beach
